nodes.title: 3 Structure And Functions In Living Organisms Part 2
Components of Blood
nodes.description: describe the composition of the blood: red blood cells, white blood cells, platelets and plasma

nodes.description: describe patterns of monohybrid inheritance using a genetic diagram

nodes.title: Transfer of Energy
nodes.description: understand the transfer of substances and energy along a food chain

nodes.title: Inheritance of Sex
nodes.description: describe the determination of the sex of offspring at fertilisation, using a genetic diagram

nodes.title: The Human Nervous System: Structure
nodes.description: understand that the central nervous system consists of the brain and spinal cord and is linked to sense organs by nerves

nodes.title: Heart Rate & Exercise
nodes.description: explain how the heart rate changes during exercise and under the influence of adrenaline

nodes.title: The Human Nervous System: Function
nodes.description:
"understand that stimulation of receptors in the sense organs sends electrical impulses
along nerves into and out of the central nervous system, resulting in rapid responses"

nodes.title: Key Terms in Ecology
nodes.description: understand the terms population, community, habitat and ecosystem

nodes.title: Heart Disease
nodes.description: understand how factors may increase the risk of developing coronary heart disease

nodes.title: Secondary Sexual Characteristics
nodes.description: understand the roles of oestrogen and testosterone in the development of secondary sexual characteristics

nodes.title: Selective Breeding in Plants
nodes.description: understand how selective breeding can develop plants with desired characteristics

nodes.title: The Human Eye: Function
nodes.description: understand the function of the eye in focusing on near and distant objects, and in responding to changes in light intensity

nodes.title: Response to Stimuli: Plants
nodes.description: understand that plants respond to stimuli

nodes.title: White Blood Cells
nodes.description: understand how the immune system responds to disease using white blood cells, illustrated by phagocytes ingesting pathogens and lymphocytes releasing antibodies specific to the pathogen

nodes.title: Abiotic & Biotic Factors
nodes.description: understand how abiotic and biotic factors affect the population size and distribution of organisms

nodes.title: Practical: Investigating Population Size
nodes.description: practical: investigate the population size of an organism in two different areas using quadrats

nodes.description: understand that plants can reproduce asexually by natural methods (illustrated by runners) and by artificial methods (illustrated by cuttings)

nodes.description: know the excretory products of the lungs, kidneys and skin (organs of excretion)

nodes.description: understand how to interpret family pedigrees

nodes.description: understand the general structure of the circulation system, including the blood vessels to and from the heart and lungs, liver and kidneys

nodes.description: understand that the genome is the entire DNA of an organism and that a gene is a section of a molecule of DNA that codes for a specific protein

nodes.description: understand the role of yeast in the production of food including bread

nodes.description: understand how an increase in greenhouse gases results in an enhanced greenhouse effect and that this may lead to global warming and its consequences

nodes.description: understand how the sex of a person is controlled by one pair of chromosomes, XX in a female and XY in a male

nodes.description: understand the biological consequences of eutrophication caused by leached minerals from fertiliser

nodes.title: The Effects of Air Pollution
nodes.description: understand the biological consequences of pollution of air by sulfur dioxide and carbon monoxide

nodes.title: The Role of Neurotransmitters
nodes.description: understand the role of neurotransmitters at synapses

nodes.title: Practical: Conditions for Germination

nodes.title: Xylem & Phloem

"describe the role of phloem in transporting sucrose and amino acids between the leaves and other parts of the plant

describe the role of xylem in transporting water and mineral ions from the roots to other parts of the plant"

nodes.title: Random Fertilisation & Genetic Variation
nodes.description: understand how random fertilisation produces genetic variation of offspring

nodes.description: understand how resistance to antibiotics can increase in bacterial populations, and appreciate how such an increase can lead to infections being difficult to control

nodes.title: Geotropic & Phototropic Responses of Plants
nodes.description: describe the geotropic and phototropic responses of roots and stems

nodes.title: Response to Change

nodes.title: Selective Breeding in Animals
nodes.description: understand how selective breeding can develop animals with desired characteristics

nodes.title: Food Webs

nodes.title: Multicellular Organisms

"describe the structure and functioning of a simple reflex arc illustrated by the
withdrawal of a finger from a hot object"

nodes.title: The Need for Excretion in Plants

nodes.description: explain Darwin’s theory of evolution by natural selection

nodes.title: Structure & Function of the Heart
nodes.description: describe the structure of the heart and how it functions

nodes.title: Human Activities & Greenhouse Gases
nodes.description: understand how human activities contribute to greenhouse gases

nodes.title: Crop Plants: Pest Control
nodes.description: understand the reasons for pest control and the advantages and disadvantages of using pesticides and biological control with crop plants

nodes.description: understand the effects on crop yield of increased carbon dioxide and increased temperature in glasshouses

nodes.title: Sexual Reproduction
nodes.description: understand the differences between sexual and asexual reproduction

nodes.description: understand the role of bacteria (Lactobacillus) in the production of yoghurt

nodes.title: The Organs of Excretion
nodes.description: know the excretory products of the lungs, kidneys and skin (organs of excretion)

nodes.title: The Human Eye: Structure
nodes.description: describe the structure and function of the eye as a receptor
